lines.text: Two days later, a royal page brought a message to our inn. Princess Mirelle wanted to meet the archer who had shot a frost-bear through the eye.
Wren went. So did I. So did Oswin, in case anyone had to be carried home.
You're the archer. Good. Can you do anything up close, or only from a tree?
Give me a stick and find out, Highness.
They fought with wooden swords. Wren was faster than anything I had ever seen. Mirelle was a wall.
Wren hit her four times in the first minute. Mirelle didn't even step back. Iron, four rings of it. Hitting her was like hitting a door.
Then Mirelle hit Wren once. Wren flew across the sand, and bounced.
Get up, Wren! She's stronger. You're faster. Make her turn!
Wren got up. She ran rings round the princess until Mirelle was turning like a millstone. Then the wind came with her, the way it had at Kesting, and her stick swept up under Mirelle's chin.
Half a heartbeat too late. Mirelle's was already at Wren's throat.
Mine. Barely. Again tomorrow?
Again tomorrow.
Then the princess sat down on the bench beside me, breathing hard, and looked at me for a long time.
Why do your people fight like they love you?
I... fix their roofs?
My uncle's knights fight like they're being paid. She fought like she'd rather die than let you down. Nobody has ever fought like that for me.
For a moment she didn't look like a princess. She looked tired, and a little lonely.
Your turn, Lord Lucan.
It was the shortest duel in the history of Aldmere.
When I opened my eyes, I was flat on my back in the sand, and she was holding out her hand. Hers was warm. Mine wasn't.
Your hands are freezing.
They always are.
Can I shoot her?
Absolutely not.
That night, Ilse came back from the College later than she ever had. She was as white as paper.
Lucan. The Stone they mean to use on you. It isn't the old one. It's new. And it's wrong.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy-four, coming soon.
